speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the appearance and specific distribution of the rash on your palms? Also, did the numbness and tingling start at the same time as the rash, or did they appear separately?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any hair loss or changes in your hair texture, and has the rash spread to other parts of your body beyond the upper body and face? I am also curious if you have experienced any muscle weakness or cramps.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on upper body and face. I also have Numbness and tingling sensation of both palms, Thinning of the eyebrows, Loss of some eyelashes, Hypopigmented macules around the elbows.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of pruritus, alopecia, and hypopigmented macules strongly suggests Pellagra, which is caused by niacin deficiency. Given your dietary habits on the rice farm, do you consume a diet heavily reliant on corn or maize with limited variety?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as a farmer, no history of travel outside the local area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Pellagra typically presents with hyperpigmentation, not hypopigmentation, so that diagnosis is unlikely. Given the hypopigmented macules, alopecia, and neurological symptoms, I suspect Hansen's disease (Leprosy). REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy
